md.areas: portions of southern Nevada into western/central Arizona
md.summary: An isolated risk for marginally severe hail, strong to locally severe wind gusts, and perhaps a landspout may accompany the strongest storms this afternoon/evening. Watch issuance is not expected.
md.discussion: Convective coverage has gradually increased through 21 UTC ahead of an approaching mid-level shortwave trough evident over southern California in recent water vapor satellite imagery. While widespread cloud cover has been prevalent across the region through much of the day, filtered diurnal heating and dewpoints ranging from the mid-50s to low-60s F are supporting weak to moderate buoyancy of 500-1000+ J/kg MLCAPE, which has been sufficient for the development of a few relatively small and transiently stronger convective cores through mid-afternoon. Stronger mid/upper flow along the eastern periphery of the aforementioned shortwave trough (~40 kts at 8-9 km MSL per the FSX/IWA VWPs) and modest mid-level lapse rates around 7 C/km may support modestly greater organization of developing updrafts and isolated marginally severe hail through mid afternoon. Isolated strong to locally severe wind gusts may also occur, primarily where stronger heating has steepened low-level lapse rates. Lastly, some potential for a brief landspout may exist given pockets of stronger low-level buoyancy overlapping ambient surface vorticity, particularly in the NV/AZ border vicinity where latest objective analysis depicts NSTP values of 1-2. Given the overall expectations for any severe risk to remain limited in magnitude and spatially isolated, watch issuance is not expected.
